newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mercedes confirms dealer's offices searched.
newsitem.headline: Mercedes confirms dealer's offices searched.

text.p: German car maker Mercedes-Benz AG on Friday confirmed that the European Commission searched some of its dealers' offices as part of an investigation into pricing and distribution.
"Mercedes headquarters in Stuttgart was not visited," a spokesman told Reuters.
The investigation sought to find out if Mercedes dealers outside of Germany refused to sell cars to German customers who crossed borders to pay local prices, the spokesman said.
Sources in Brussels told reporters earlier on Friday that the EU competition watchdog had raided offices at Mercedes and General Motors Corp.'s Adam Opel AG unit.

News of the raids emerged as the Commission released details of car price differences across 12 of the 15 EU nations. The Commission said parallel trade in cars -- when customers go to other countries for lower prices -- was being blocked in Germany, Belgium, Spain and the Netherlands.
The raids involving Mercedes were related to sales in all four countries, while those involving Opel were related only to Dutch sales, the source said.
